new_rows.what the ink shows: The abbreviation begins with a small upturned entry and a long, low, compressed connecting stroke, then rises into the prominent f-stroke, which drops below the line and returns diagonally upward. A separate small raised t with a short rightward cross/foot follows immediately. There is no further baseline letter group between that f and the raised t: no separate o loop or r/m shoulders survive there. The large diagonal cancellation crosses the early compressed prefix, not the gap after f. The surviving abbreviation is unift; uniformt would supply an unrepresented orm sequence. The exact internal uni gestures are highly compressed, so confidence is medium rather than high.

After the underlined commutative, the word has a shallow initial hook and long connected low prefix leading into a tall descending f with an upward return. The next separate mark is the small raised terminal t; the following full-height stroke begins fermée. No baseline o/r/m group intervenes between f and t. In the same page's earlier fully written uniforme, the corresponding f gesture is followed by a distinct additional low connected letter group extending rightward; that group is absent from M0335. This independently supports the shorter written abbreviation unift, without expansion to uniformt. The prefix's internal letter separations are compressed, which limits confidence to medium.
